title: Aurora IL Heat Pump Rebates 2026: ComEd Discounts and What Nicor Gas Covers
desc: Aurora, Illinois heat pump rebates in 2026: ComEd takes up to $2,000 off a ducted heat pump, and Nicor Gas pays only for gas equipment. Most Aurora homes are owner-occupied and gas-heated.
h1: Heat Pump Rebates in Aurora, Illinois
lead: Aurora gets electricity from ComEd and gas from Nicor Gas. For a heat pump, ComEd is the one that pays. Nicor Gas rebates are only for gas equipment that replaces gas equipment, so they will not help with a heat pump. About two in three Aurora households own their home, and most live in a house rather than a large building. Here are the amounts we confirmed on October 6, 2026.
cards_heading: Heat pump money for Aurora homes in 2026
cards_intro: Amounts and rules below are from ComEd's and Nicor Gas's own pages.

cards.title: ComEd ducted heat pump
cards.note: Discount on your installer's invoice. The amount depends on size (under or over 2.5 tons) and efficiency tier.

cards.title: ComEd ductless mini-split
cards.note: For rooms or additions without ducts. Must meet the higher efficiency level.

cards.title: ComEd thermostat add-on
cards.note: An extra $75 when your heat pump contractor installs an ENERGY STAR smart thermostat with the heat pump.

cards.title: Nicor Gas furnace rebate
cards.note: Only if you replace a gas furnace with a better gas furnace. It is not for heat pumps.

cards.title: ComEd Whole Home Electric
cards.note: Income-eligible homes. 2026 money for gas-heated homes is allocated, and the program is expected to reopen in January 2027.

cards.title: Federal home energy credit
cards.note: No federal heat pump credit after December 31, 2025.

after_cards: ComEd's heat pump page says no application is needed. A ComEd heat pump-trained contractor applies the discount on the invoice, and a self-install does not qualify.
sections: The Census Bureau's survey for 2020 to 2024 counts 63,763 homes in Aurora. Owners are 66.4% of households and renters 33.6%. Detached houses are 58.7% of homes and attached houses 16.6%. Buildings of two to four homes are 8.7%. A landlord's approval matters for only about a third of households. The City of Aurora's own electric aggregation page confirms that ComEd delivers electricity in Aurora.

Utility gas heats 82.5% of Aurora homes and electricity 14.8%. Bottled gas heats 1.5% and fuel oil 0.2%. For the gas-heated majority, a heat pump can replace the air conditioner and cut furnace use. Some owners keep the furnace for the coldest days. ComEd's page does not require the furnace to be removed, but it does require the heat pump to be installed by a trained contractor.

Nicor's furnace rebate is for gas replacing gas, so choose between them for the same job. A new gas furnace earns $150 or $225. A heat pump earns a ComEd discount. Compare total cost, not only the rebate.

Aurora's stock is younger than Chicago's. The survey says 42.5% of homes were built before 1980 and 13.5% before 1940, while 24.8% were built since 2000. Newer homes often have ducts, which suits a ducted heat pump and the higher ComEd tiers. Older homes may need duct repairs or a mini-split. Ask your installer to test duct leakage, and consider sealing with the Nicor Gas air sealing rebate of $500 first.

ComEd's top tier needs 17 SEER2 and 8.5 HSPF2 for a ducted unit. For a unit of 2.5 tons or more the discount can reach $2,000. Smaller units reach $1,500. A mini-split needs 17 SEER2 and 9.0 HSPF2. SEER2 is the cooling score and HSPF2 is the heating score. Ask for the AHRI certificate number, which proves the ratings.

If your household income is at or below 80% of the area median, call ComEd at 855-433-2700 for a free assessment. Households at or below 200% of the federal poverty level can apply for the state's free weatherization program. Our Illinois guide lists the limits.
claim_heading: How to get a heat pump rebate in Aurora
claim_steps: Confirm ComEd is your electric company.
Get quotes from ComEd heat pump-trained contractors.
Ask which tier your unit earns and have it written on the quote.
Have the contractor add the thermostat for the extra $75 if you want one.
Check Nicor's air sealing rebate before the install.

faq: How much does ComEd pay for a heat pump in Aurora?
Up to $900 to $2,000 for a ducted unit and up to $500 to $1,000 for a mini-split.
Does Nicor Gas pay for a heat pump?
No. Nicor's rebates replace gas equipment with gas equipment.
Do I have to remove my gas furnace?
ComEd's page does not require it. Ask your contractor and Nicor before you decide.
Is the federal tax credit available?
Can renters in Aurora get this?
The person who pays for the work does. Renters are 33.6% of Aurora households, so a tenant needs the owner to agree.
